items.ownerBrief:
DECIDE: does the licence scope grammar's `grantee scope` axis (11.08.01 D-15 — 'the licensee plus permitted assignees/sublicensees, bounded by a stated purpose') give a rights holder a place to key a BUYER BLOCK, or is it grant-side only?

Why it is yours: two owning files carry opposed, self-consistent decisions. 11.08.01 D-15 makes party identity an axis of the grammar. 11.04.02 D-09 splits blocks into two key spaces precisely because 'the grammar has no counterparty axis', and 11.04.03's fold, the domain CX's CX-16/CX-18 and rejected pair R-08 all rest on that premise. Resolving it changes what an owner can express and when a block takes effect.

OPTION A — grantee scope is grant-side only (RECOMMENDED). It says who THIS instrument runs to; it is not a value space an owner authors refusals in. Buyer blocks stay outside the grammar, evaluated at request time; D-09, CX-16, CX-18 and R-08 all stand unchanged; nothing else in 11.04 moves. It matches the axis's stated purpose — 11.08.01 DT-15 argues it from DELIVERY failure (an agency licence that does not run to the brand is worthless paper), never from refusal. Cost: the grammar carries an axis that policies deliberately ignore, which must be written down or the next auditor finds the same contradiction.

OPTION B — grantee scope is policy-keyable. An owner expresses 'never BrandCo' as a grantee-axis exclusion (11.08.01 D-05 permits exclusion), buyer blocks fold like category blocks and become evaluable at authoring time. Consequences that come with it, none of them small: catalogue availability changes for buyers who have not asked yet (D-09's second clause dies); 11.04.03's fold must operate over identity, which CX-18 calls structurally impossible because identity is not a lattice point; and 11.04.02 D-10's 'no corporate-ownership inference' now sits inside the grammar rather than beside it.

UNOWNED CONSEQUENCE EITHER WAY: 11.08.01 D-04 makes an unset axis `unspecified` and fails containment. If grantee is an axis of every scope point, a policy that never names a grantee contains no request at all — so under Option A the grammar needs an explicit rule that policies do not carry the grantee axis, and under Option B every policy must set it. Neither file says which today.

Where it is tracked: 11.04.02 Q-07 (User, /create-prd), referenced from 11.04.01 Behavior, 11.04.02 Cross-Cut Notes and music-licensing-cx.md CX-16.
